# Roadmap

Part of the [app_registry product brief](../PRODUCT.md).

Each `Cn` below is defined in [`02-capability-map.md`](02-capability-map.md).

_`Status` is each milestone's **current** delivery status, derived from krill's append-only `milestone_status_event` history (`store.MilestoneStatusEventStore.CurrentStatuses`). A milestone with no recorded transition is `not started` — that is krill's own derivation from the absence of history, not a rendered default._

6 milestones (0 abandoned), one block each below.

### M0 — Baseline: CI records every artifact, operators promote and roll back through the registry with full SCD2 history, see per-promotion health, and drive whole releases from a live web UI.

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9, C13

Retroactive baseline recorded at krill onboarding (2026-11-14). App Registry was mature before it had a product brief: phases AR-M through AR-8 and beyond (see `tools/app_registry/PLAN-HISTORY.md`) shipped all of these capabilities before krill tracked them. This milestone exists so that shipped work has a delivering milestone. It was never designed or planned as a krill milestone.

C9 is delivered here at per-promotion granularity. The environment-level aggregate is a separate Requirement under C9, and M1 delivers it.

### M1 — A release operator can see, at a glance, whether an entire environment is healthy right now

- Status: not started
- Must not foreclose: LB2
- Deliberately deferred: Automatic rollback action [C10] (→ M2); Approval gate [C11] (→ M3)
- FR budget: 12

Delivers (a Requirement; the renderer's Delivers line lists capabilities only): C9 — "Environment-level aggregate health view". C9 itself shipped at per-promotion granularity in M0. This milestone closes its one remaining gap, environment-level aggregation, on top of what has already shipped.

Design note (not load-bearing, flagged by architect): build the aggregation as a query/view over `promotion_sync_event`. Do not subscribe to the RabbitMQ SSE bus for "live" data. LB3 calls out this trap for C10, and it applies here too, even though a stale aggregate view is not a broken trigger.

### M2 — A release operator no longer has to manually roll back a bad promotion

- Status: not started
- Delivers: C10
- Must not foreclose: LB2, LB3
- Deliberately deferred: Approval gate [C11] (→ M3)
- FR budget: 12

App Registry rolls back to the prior artifact automatically when the environment health view from M1 says the new one isn't healthy. The decision policy reads `promotion_sync_event` and does not widen `promotion_event`'s enum (LB2). The trigger comes from the durable Temporal/writeback path, never from the RabbitMQ SSE bus (LB3).

### M3 — A promotion attempt generates a trackable approval-request scoped to (environment, build), and only executes once that request is resolved

- Status: not started
- Delivers: C11
- Must not foreclose: LB1, LB4
- Deliberately deferred: Ephemeral/per-PR environments [C12] (→ Later, unscheduled); Release-trigger-layer approval stub's disposition (worker/release/approval.go CheckApproval) — no capability number of its own, not folded into C11 (see LB1) (→ Open question beyond this brief)
- FR budget: 12

Promoting a build to an environment creates a first-class approval-request artifact, replacing a boolean gate checked inline in the promote call. The promotion itself happens downstream of resolving that request (approve or reject). Scoped to the promotion-layer seam only (LB1). Approver identity is a Keycloak role check through the existing `server/auth`/`grpcauth` model (LB4).

FR budget 12 depends on design intake resolving:
- whether one approval-request covers a given (environment, build) pair exactly once, or every promotion attempt;
- whether a rejected request can be re-requested;
- whether the request is visible/actionable from the same UI surface as promotions;
- (architect flag) how to represent a pending request without reusing the `promotion` table's SCD2 row. `promotion_current_idx` is unique per (environment, target/app), which is coarser than per-build. An unapproved build's row would otherwise show up as "currently deployed" via `v_current_promotion`, which M1's health view and M2's rollback decision both consume.

### M4 — CI and other consumers resolve which artifact kinds exist and how to acquire them entirely from the registry, with no hardcoded tool-name list left anywhere in CI

- Status: not started
- Delivers: C15
- Must not foreclose: LB5
- Deliberately deferred: CAS storage, dedup, and blob-level content identity for CLI binaries [C14] (→ M5)
- FR budget: 12

Layered over the existing S3 location-based publish/resolve path, with no storage changes. Removes the three hardcoded call sites: the release workflow (`.github/workflows/release-v2.yml`), `.github/actions/download-release-tools/action.yml`, and the `cliBinaryTargets` map in `worker/release/finalize.go`.

Does not touch promotion, approval, or the health/sync path (LB1–LB4). Binary-kind artifacts already use the same kind-agnostic `promotion` table that M1 and M2 build on. So this milestone's kind/acquisition-resolution logic must not assume `artifact.digest` is a content hash for binary kind. Today it isn't one, and it won't be until M5 lands (LB5).

OCI-based publishing (images/charts, C1) stays on its existing GHCR path, untouched.

### M5 — CI publishes a CLI binary (and any future non-OCI artifact kind) to durable storage through one content-addressed, registry-brokered path

- Status: not started
- Delivers: C14
- Must not foreclose: LB5
- Deliberately deferred: Firmware as a fully-wired second non-OCI kind — C14's extension point only needs to be generic enough that firmware needs no new publish/resolve code when it lands (→ Later, unscheduled)
- FR budget: 12

This is not a greenfield build. `worker/release/finalize.go`'s `binaryUploaderFor`/`cliBinaryS3Key` is a live, non-CAS upload path in production today. It holds real `RELEASE_TOOLS_S3_*` credentials and uploads directly to a location-keyed S3 path, with no presigned broker and no dedup. It already populates `artifact.digest` for binary-kind artifacts (`recordCLIBinaryArtifact`: the `sha256` of `checksums.txt`, not a hash of any single stored object's bytes). Design intake needs a real migration path for what is already published under the old convention, for example backfilling existing binary artifacts into the new CAS scheme, or dual-reading old-convention objects during a cutover window.

This milestone makes LB5's identity decision (what gets hashed, which digest-string format), the one choice this brief flags as expensive to reverse.

Not carried forward: the pre-cutover key-derivation and dual-write/back-compat machinery in the shape #1142 proposed (its H8, section H). There is a real migration to design, but not that one.

FR budget 12: size it against the migration above, not a greenfield build.

Sequencing: M4 and M5 were appended after M3 rather than reordered ahead of it. Their placement relative to M1–M3 is a placeholder and a call for human review.
